title: Scientific Opinion on Dietary Reference Values for cobalamin (vitamin B12)
authors: EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition, and Allergies (NDA)
funder: European Food Safety Authority, on request from the European Commission (question EFSA-Q-2011-01227); preparatory work by the EFSA Working Group on Dietary Reference Values for vitamins and EFSA staff.
result: A combination of biomarkers of cobalamin status, namely serum cobalamin, holotranscobalamin, methylmalonic acid and plasma total homocysteine, was judged the most suitable basis for Dietary Reference Values; an Average Requirement could not be determined. Adequate Intake for adults 4 ug/day, based on biomarker data and observed mean intakes of 4.2 to 8.6 ug/day in adults in several EU countries; 4.5 ug/day in pregnancy and 5 ug/day in lactation; 1.5 ug/day at 7 to 11 months rising to 4 ug/day at 15 to 17 years.
